_note: PLAN.md 9. All numbers are STARTING VALUES to be tuned by playtest.
MVP is three nodes (PLAN.md 10): chop wood, mine gold, hunt a deer. Stone,
farms, fishing, berries and boar are 6.5.
`amounts` is indexed by SimResourceNode.size_class (0 small, 1 medium,
2 large), and so is `visuals`: SIZE PICKS THE SPRITE as well as the amount, as
of 2026-08-17. It did not for months -- the note here used to say the visual
difference 'earns nothing at sprite scale' -- and that was exactly the
complaint the ore request was raised over: a 200-gold seam and an 800-gold
seam were pixel-identical, so a player could not tell a rich node from a poor
one and the size classes were data nobody could act on. Eight bakes later they
read apart at a glance.
`visuals` is optional and CLAMPS when short, which is not a convenience but a
requirement: the roster names three ore actors and only TWO rock actors, so
stone's medium and large deliberately share the quarry. A kind that omits the
list entirely (food, wood, the animals) draws its one `visual` at every size.
`footprints` is the same idea for the GROUND a node claims, and the project
owner's rule for it is 'for trees it makes sense, for stone and gold it does
not' (2026-08-17). A one-tile footprint under a 244 px seam let units walk
through the middle of solid rock and buildings go up where the player can
plainly see a mine, so the mined kinds now claim what their art covers.
Matched through the projection visuals.json documents: a footprint of (Fx, Fy)
TILES draws a diamond (Fx + Fy) * 32 px wide, so the number to hit is the
sprite's own width. gold 95 / 180 / 244 px wants 3.0 / 5.6 / 7.6 tiles of
diamond, which rounds to 1x1, 3x3 and 4x4 -- the small seam is nearer 1x1 (64
px) than 2x2 (128), and staying at one tile also leaves every fixture that
spawns a small mine alone. Stone is 72 and 270 px: 1x1 and 4x4, and its medium
shares the large actor so it shares the large footprint.
TREES STAY AT ONE TILE deliberately. An oak is 232 px of canopy over a trunk
that really does stand on a single tile; claiming 4x4 for each would turn a
twelve-tree forest into an impassable wall, and the canopy overhang is handled
where it belongs -- Occlusion.column_pad_for, which pads only the difference
between what the art covers and what the entity claims.
`pick_footprints` is the SAME SHAPE and a different question: not what ground
the node holds but where a finger may land to hit it. Nothing in the sim reads
it -- it feeds GameView._covers and nothing else -- so widening one does not
widen the other. Only the tree sets it (2x2), and it is short on purpose: the
list clamps, so one entry covers all three size classes.
It exists because of the tap the project owner reported on 2026-08-23. A tree
is 232 px of art standing on one 64x32 tile, so the trunk you aim at is a tile
and a half up-screen from the tile that actually answers the tap, and you miss.
The two-tile box reaches up-screen automatically, because _covers takes the rect
as `centre - footprint / 2`. Note this does NOT contradict the paragraph above:
the tree still CLAIMS one tile, a forest is still walkable, and the change is
invisible to pathing, placement, occlusion and depth sort alike.
Small nodes -- the bush, the sheep, the deer -- get nothing here. Their art is
not tall enough for a second tile to be the right shape, and they are covered
instead by GameView.TAP_REACH_PX, which lets a tap that hits bare ground fall
back to the nearest one-tile node's ARTWORK. See pick().
WOOD goes the other way. The roster names four tree species at 500 each -- one
amount, four looks -- which is not a size class at all but the `variants` axis
in visuals.json: vis.tree lists itself plus elm, teak and toona, and each tree
picks one from the tile it stands on. So a forest is mixed species where a gold
seam is graded by richness, and the two mechanisms stay separate because they
answer different questions.
THE DEER LEFT THIS FILE at 6.1b (2026-08-23) and is `unit.deer` now. It carried
`wildlife: { roam_radius: 6, flees: true }` here for months and NOTHING EVER READ
IT -- and nothing could have: roaming needs MovementSystem, which moves SimUnit
and skips nodes, so the data sat on a class physically unable to act on it. What
is left behind is res.deer_carcass, and vis.deer_carcass is finally drawing the
thing it was baked for rather than sitting unreferenced.
A deer is therefore HUNTED now, not harvested: it wanders, it bolts when hit, and
the 140 food is in the body afterwards. The berry bush remains the easy opening
food (6.1a's substitution stands) and sheep and cattle still stand still to be
taken, so nothing forces a player to hunt before they want to.
res.berry_bush stands in for the MVP food node for now (session decision):
it needs no hunt/kill/carcass state machine at all -- gather it like a tree
-- and vis.berry_bush is fully delivered with a real atlas, unlike the deer
carcass gap above. res.deer is left defined but unused rather than deleted,
in case wildlife hunting (6.1a/6.1b) comes back later.
res.stone, res.sheep and res.cattle were added 2026-08-17, wiring art that had
been staged and referenced by nothing. STONE is the one that was a real bug
rather than unused art: every building costs stone and the HUD counts it, but
no node on any map yielded any, so the only stone a player could ever have was
MapGen's starting handout. The villager already carries a stone gather_rate and
carry_cap, and the town centre and mining camp already accept a stone drop-off
-- nothing needed building, the node kind simply did not exist. PLAN.md 6.5.
Its amounts MATCH GOLD rather than the roster's own 1000/5000/10000 (Age & Unit
Planning.md ORE). Those are 0 A.D.'s figures and every amount in this file is
well below them; stone and gold are the two mined kinds, four slots each, so
matching them is one fewer number to tune blind.
SHEEP and CATTLE take the roster's own amounts (100 and 500 -- cattle is one
animal worth a lot, which is 0 A.D.'s balance and reads fine here). Both are
gathered like a berry bush and neither carries a `wildlife` block: they stand
still and are harvested, which needs no hunt/kill/carcass machinery. Both are
SINGLE-SIZE for the reason the deer is -- a flock of differently-sized sheep
reads as an art bug, not as variety.
THE PREDATORS ARE NOT IN THIS FILE. Wolf, boar and bear are all `unit.*` in
units.json, because a thing that chases needs a task, a path, a facing and a
cooldown and every one of those lives on SimUnit. What IS here is the three
carcasses they drop -- the only nodes in the game spawned by a death rather than
by MapGen (DeathSystem), which is the seam where a hunted thing becomes a
harvested one.
res.boar was briefly a harvestable node (2026-08-23, morning) and stopped being
one the same day: the project owner's call is that boar and bear both FIGHT BACK,
which is what a real one does and what 0 A.D. models. So the 150 food that used
to be standing in a field is now inside something that charges.
Amounts: 30 / 150 / 300 for wolf / boar / bear. The wolf and bear are the
roster's own figures; the boar's 150 is a judgement, since Age & Unit Planning.md
lists no pig. The spread is the point -- a wolf is barely worth butchering and a
bear is a prize worth losing a villager over. gather_slots rises with the animal
for the same reason: three people can work a bear and only one a wolf.
ALL THREE DRAW vis.deer_carcass, temporarily. Only the deer's carcass is baked;
vis.wolf_carcass is requested and vis.boar_carcass and vis.bear_carcass are not
yet. A dead deer where a dead bear should be reads as the wrong animal -- but
pointing at an undeclared id would draw the magenta unknown AND fail the
no-load-warnings test, so the wrong animal is the better of the two. One line
each when the bakes land.
STILL NOT WIRED: the fish, and it is a feature rather than a wiring gap.
`spawn_resource_node` calls `can_place_building`, which hard-codes Domain.LAND and
would refuse a fish on shallow water; unit.fishing_ship carries empty gather_rate
and carry_cap; and nothing treats building.dock as a drop-off. Baked, staged and
declared in visuals.json, and waiting on all three of those.
